findings: Reindexing the full unaveraged ideal-class sum under an Artin element multiplies it by the quadratic character (inverse equals itself). With the retained CM reciprocity action and Q-defined parametrization this is exact point equality, so kernel descent and anti-invariance hold before torsion removal.

For D>1 the actual positive squarefree D and negative h* yield the biquadratic field. The automorphism tau over K_D changes both square roots. The D-twist isomorphism changes sign under tau; hence its inverse sends Gamma_D exactly onto E^(D)(K_D). The rational D-character subgroup is the image of E^(D)(Q).

Over Q, the rationalized Mordell-Weil group of E^(D) over K_D decomposes into E^(D) and E^(D*D*h*)=E^(h*) parts by sum and difference. The assumed rank-zero latter part implies sigma fixes every torsion-free class. This is not a claim that sigma fixes every point.

For every Q in E^(D)(K_D), Q+sigma(Q) is actually rational and has class 2[Q]. Thus the rational subgroup image contains 2 Lambda_D. Under the separately retained rank-one premise its index divides two. No torsion-free splitting or division by two integrally is required.

D=1 uses the actual quadratic K=Q(sqrt(h*)) and ordinary E(K), with rational E and rank-zero E^(h*) parts. The genus character is the stipulated trivial one. The same norm argument applies; no nonexistent biquadratic automorphism is used.

This supplies the native GENUS lattice in the stated caller. It neither proves the separate ring-class lattice assertion in3308 nor supplies the CM/genus character identification, analytic rank-one theorem, height formula, or uniform torsion annihilator.
